title: bug: cloud-init 26.1's ssh_authkey_fingerprints creates an empty authorized_keys for both job identities, so readiness fails IDENTITY_LOGIN_ENABLED on every real boot
description:
Found by governor-ce2f28b9 on 2026-10-31 in R13's second Linux certify run, the first after 62a909c1's mounts fix. That run passed provision, failed readiness with IDENTITY_LOGIN_ENABLED, and passed teardown; report ~/moe-certify/certification-linux-x64-20261031T204637Z-c53779.json, never recorded. It blocks R13 certification on every platform, because every platform boots the same user-data.

**Reproduction, on real guests, 20:50-20:56Z.** Multipass 1.17.0 snap (qemu) in WSL2, the pinned x64 image (sha256 04e8f246…), cloud-init 26.1-0ubuntu1~24.04.1. User-data was built by buildUserData from the real guest-supervisor.py (3a19f3bf…) and a random 32-byte credential, launched with certify's argv.
- Guest A, today's user-data:
  - cloud-init ends `done`/`done` with no errors, which confirms 62a909c1's fix;
  - but `/home/moe-agent/.ssh/authorized_keys` and `/home/moe-check/.ssh/authorized_keys` EXIST, mode 600, **0 bytes**;
  - the readiness probe `keys:<id>`, which is `sudo -n test -e /home/<id>/.ssh/authorized_keys` (guest-readiness.mjs identityChecks), exits 0 for both, which gives IDENTITY_LOGIN_ENABLED.
- Every other readiness probe passed on guest A when run by hand: mountinfo, layout, the supervisor, shim and tools digests, locked passwd status, groups, all 10 DENIED read/write probes, and sudo denied. `keys:` is the only readiness blocker.

**Cause.** cloud-init 26.1's `cc_ssh_authkey_fingerprints` runs in modules-final. For every user in `users`, it calls `ssh_util.extract_authorized_keys(user)`, which creates an empty authorized_keys file. Log, guest A:
- `20:52:03,987 Running module ssh_authkey_fingerprints`
- `20:52:03,988 Writing to /home/moe-agent/.ssh/authorized_keys - wb: [600] 0 bytes`
- the same for moe-check.
The file grants no login, but it trips the strict existence probe on every clean boot.

**Proven direction (the planner decides).** Adding `no_ssh_fingerprints: true` to the cloud-config makes the module return before it touches any key file: cc_ssh_authkey_fingerprints.py:107 in the guest, `if util.is_true(cfg.get("no_ssh_fingerprints", False)): … return`.
- `cloud-init schema -c` (WSL 26.1) reports the amended user-data as "Valid schema".
- Guest B, the same user-data plus `no_ssh_fingerprints: true` right after `disable_root: true`:
  - cloud-init ends `done`/`done`, errors [];
  - the log has "Skipping module named ssh_authkey_fingerprints" once;
  - neither job identity has an authorized_keys file;
  - the default user's Multipass key is intact;
  - every readiness probe passes, including keys:moe-agent and keys:moe-check at rc=1.
- Both guests were deleted by exact name.
- The module only logs key fingerprints to the console, so turning it off loses nothing Moe uses.

**Sequencing.** This row dependsOn 4679ec68, because both edit scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs. After both are DONE, the governor re-runs certify: Linux first, then Windows.
definitionOfDone: The cloud-config emitted by buildUserData prevents cloud-init from creating any authorized_keys file for moe-agent and moe-check, for example with `no_ssh_fingerprints: true`. It validates under cloud-init 26.1: `cloud-init schema -c <emitted user-data file>`, using WSL /usr/bin/cloud-init 26.1-0ubuntu1~24.04.1, reports it valid with no schema errors. The evidence names the command and its output.

Readiness strictness is unchanged. The keys:<id> probe still treats an existing authorized_keys, even an empty one, as IDENTITY_LOGIN_ENABLED, and the existing readiness rows pass unedited. The change says in a comment why the construct keeps the job identities free of key files on cloud-init 26.1.
A regression test fails on the old user-data and passes on the new one. The local-runner.test.mjs user-data pin is updated.

scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py is byte-unchanged (sha256 3a19f3bf07cf6d47a1fb93e425b4bf7f1eb7e2b3b2d31bb21ba00752ecef8190), so R13's commit-under-test pin still holds. The local-runner suite passes in a git-archive snapshot under env -i with the pinned Node, not in place.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen: the top-level cloud-config key no_ssh_fingerprints: true (the governor's proven direction). It is schema-valid on 26.1; handle returns before it reads any user; user-data outranks vendor and system config; governor guest B booted done/done with no job-identity key file, the default user's Multipass key intact and every readiness probe passing. Rejected: per-user no_create_home or system (the module's per-user skip at line 117), which drops the job identities' home dirs or turns them into system accounts; overriding cloud_final_modules, which replaces the image's whole final-stage list; a runcmd that deletes the files, which hides the write instead of preventing it and races module order; and loosening keys:<id>, which a task rail forbids.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: buildUserData's `lines` array is the only source of the cloud-config. Only scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs pins its text (the 'buildUserData renders...' test and UD1). UD1 keeps working unedited: its `mounts` replace still matches, because the mounts line now follows the new key. The readiness row 'authorized keys' (keys:<id> exit 0 maps to IDENTITY_LOGIN_ENABLED) is the strictness proof and stays unedited. The dependency task-4679ec68 edits the same test file in its provisioning section (about line 1675 on), away from the CQ-R07 bootstrap tests (about lines 1121-1181), and never touches guest-bootstrap.mjs.
planningNotes.risks: UD2 leans on cloud-init 26.1 internals. It is gated to exactly 26.1, like UD1, and any renamed symbol fails it instead of skipping. On any other cloud-init version both UD1 and UD2 skip, so the real-guest proof stays the governor's R13 certify re-run (Linux first, then Windows). local-runner.test.mjs is a contested path: edit it only with the Edit/Write tools. The size is about 40 lines across 2 files under normal sizing; this is a separate bug row, not growth of the CQ-R07 exception.
